Theme

Body, health & movement

itch verb and noun

also itching, pruritus

classical

Traupman 335

prūriō, prūrīre

verb, fourth conjugation

itch; also figuratively long for something

The ancient dictionary does not supply a perfect or supine; regular-looking perfects are not presented as verified principal parts. The verb’s further etymology is uncertain.

Other words

  • prūrītus, prūrītūs m. — itching

    noun, fourth declension · classical

    English medical pruritus derives from the Latin noun.

  • prūrīgō, prūrīginis f. — itching, irritation

    noun, third declension · also used · classical

  • prūriēns, prūrientis — itching

    also used · classical

Examples

  • Mihi bracchium prūrit.

    My arm itches.composed

  • Ubi tibi prūrit?

    Where does it itch?composed

See also scratch, mange.

SourcesLewis & Short: prurio · Lewis & Short: pruritus · Lewis & Short: prurigo

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
